newsitem.title: JAPAN: Inflation risk smaller than recovery risk--BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Inflation risk smaller than recovery risk--BOJ.

text.p: The risk of inflation in Japan is small compared with the risk that the economy will not be able to get on a firm, self-sustainable recovery path, a senior Bank of Japan (BOJ) official said on Tuesday.
"If we weigh inflationary risks and the risk of a fiscal drag undermining the potential for a self-sustainable economic recovery, the latter would be greater," he told Reuters.
He said although the potential was high for Japan to achieve a self-sustainable recovery, it was not ensured.
The central bank reflects this observation in its management of monetary policy, he added.
The official said economic indicators which gauge the health of the service sector, which has a bigger role than goods in Japan's overall economy, are not yet strong.
In contrast, indicators for manufactured goods have been strong, but that could change due to such variables as foreign exchange rates, he said.

In Japanese money markets, there is upward pressure on short-term interest rates partly due to expectations that the BOJ may eventually tighten its credit grip mildly in view of recent signs of recovery.
The key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) rate rose to 0.60 percent on Tuesday, the highest since August 20, 1996, traders said.
